Hey Alice —

Short answers: yes, we return 429 with a Retry-After header for standard rate-limit rejections. For transient errors (5xx) treat them similarly with exponential backoff and jitter. Below is the recommended pattern we ship in our SDKs and samples. I'll attach a tiny Python/Node snippet — putting Node inline since that's your primary runtime.

Node (pseudo-code):

const MAX_RETRIES = 5;
const BASE_DELAY_MS = 200; // start 200ms

async function callRedwood(payload) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < MAX_RETRIES) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(endpoint, { body: JSON.stringify(payload) });
      if (res.status === 429) {
        const ra = res.headers.get('Retry-After');
        const wait = ra ? parseInt(ra) * 1000 : Math.min(10000, BASE_DELAY_MS * Math.pow(2, attempt));
        await sleep(wait + jitter());
        attempt++;
        continue;
      }
      if (res.status >= 500) {
        await sleep(Math.min(10000, BASE_DELAY_MS * Math.pow(2, attempt)) + jitter());
        attempt++;
        continue;
      }
      return res.json();
    } catch (err) {
      // network / TLS errors
      await sleep(Math.min(10000, BASE_DELAY_MS * Math.pow(2, attempt)) + jitter());
      attempt++;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Max retries exceeded');
}

Key notes: use full jitter (random 0..base) combined with exponential backoff, cap at ~10s, and stop after 4-6 attempts. Also use per-request timeouts (e.g., 5s for short calls, configurable) — avoiding unbounded socket hangs.

I also uploaded a small sample file: sdk_retry_examples.py with the same pattern for other teams.

Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Following up with the cutover proposal based on your staged rollout preference. Proposed windows (slack-window for coordination + DNS TTL considerations):

- Dry-run (internal smoke) — Nov 24, 02:00-03:00 UTC (no DNS changes).
- Canary 10% — Nov 28, 01:00-04:00 UTC (monitor p95 latency, error rates).
- Canary 50% — Dec 1, 01:00-04:00 UTC.
- Full cutover 100% — Dec 3, 01:00-06:00 UTC.

Operational notes:
- We'll provision a canary routing rule in the Redwood gateway to route X% of traffic to the new customer model. That avoids DNS until full cutover.
- If canary error rate exceeds 2x baseline or p95 latency increases > 250ms, we'll pause and rollback automatically.
- For your firewall team: we can provide a small set of egress IPs plus a DNS name to resolve to the live endpoints; we'll confirm IP list once the dedicated pool is allocated.

Attached: cutover_window_schedule.csv (timeline + on-call list). Also linking the HubSpot runbook for the rollout: https://hubspot.company/contacts/OLV-42

Grace O'Connor

Alice / team —

Great questions; short answers and next steps below.

1) SLA & procurement packet: attaching a one-pager and the procurement contact card in the shared Drive. Procurement, meet James Ortiz (j.ortiz@redwood.com) who will handle invoicing and PO intake.

2) Throttling impact during canary: there will be no QPS reduction for other tenants. Our routing isolates canary traffic to reserved capacity slices for Dedicated customers. If you are on Hosted with shared pools, we'll allocate soft reservations and enforce hard per-customer quotas to prevent cross-tenant interference.

3) Expected downtime for DNS-based cutover: typically 0–30s for requests in flight, plus a potential DNS TTL propagation tail depending on your TTL settings. Because you're doing gateway-based canary, real user impact should be negligible; we still recommend a 1–5 minute rollback window as a precaution.

4) Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 60min technical walkthrough for Nov 24 09:00 PST to go through SDK samples, the retry pattern Ben provided, and the smoke-test checklist.
- Ben will share the Gist with the Node sample by EOD tomorrow.
- Grace will confirm egress IP list and attach it to the HubSpot runbook.
